topicName: youth and education in nazi germany

steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The Hitler Youth was made compulsory by law on 1 December 1936. By 1939, over 8.7 million young people (over 90% of eligible youth) were members. The organisation aimed to indoctrinate young Germans with Nazi ideology and prepare boys for military service. | Key Fact: The Bund Deutscher Mädel (BDM) was the girls' equivalent of the Hitler Youth. By 1939, it had over 2 million members. The BDM focused on physical fitness, domestic skills, and motherhood training - preparing girls to be healthy mothers for the Aryan race. | Key Fact: The BDM emphasised that a woman's highest duty was to bear healthy Aryan children.
